steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Please wait here for a moment. We'll have someone bring you the contract.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: All the fine points of this collaboration are detailed in here. Please bring it back and have the Count read it over.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: If you have any other questions, please feel free to ask... Miss Carnelian? Are you listening?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Oh... Sorry, I spaced out a little.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: So, as I was saying, do you have any questions about this collaboration?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Not for the moment. I will bring this back to Count Hohenlohe so that he may make his decision.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Wonderful. I look forward to the Count arriving at a decision that will benefit us both.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Are you leaving already? If you have no other plans, Sir Feuerbach told me to accompany...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: You needn't worry. Do let Sir Feuerbach know how thankful I am for his generosity.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Since I am here, I will take a stroll around the city to see the sights.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Ah, would you like a guide, then? I can arrange for one right away.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Please don't worry yourself. I will just be strolling about.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Oh, this reminds me... I visited before when I represented the Count on our last collaboration. I believe that was before the Empresses' last banquet?

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Precisely.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: If I remember correctly, this place was filled with the horns of other species as decorations. Are we trying out new style?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Hmm, take this ornament for example. You don't see its quality and lustrousness every day. If I have to guess, they must be made from Solidified Origincrystals.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: That is correct.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Miss Carnelian, I must say, you have a good eye, and far more so than before.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: You flatter me.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: As far as I know, stable crystals such as these can only be mined in the deepest parts of Originium veins, and most of them are buried inside the Originium itself. That makes them extraordinarily rare.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: And these crystals are far harder than stone. Normal carving processes cannot so much as make a dent on them.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Considering the difficulty of the process, I suppose it must have taken Sir Feuerbach some effort to amass such a massive collection of fine decorations?

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: It's not actually that difficult. Master Feuerbach found this collection of Originium art pieces by coincidence when he diligently inspected his territory.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: He thought that their black luster is full of appeal and mystique, making them prime for viewing, and so he had us place them here so that they may be appreciated by all our visitors.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: In that case, I guess we should raise a glass to his generosity.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Miss Carnelian, you seem to be familiar with the subject.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: I can't say I'm familiar with them... Though... Hm... I've seen how these are produced before, so it does stir my emotions a little.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Take a look at this. For just a small chunk of Origincrystal like this, you must dig several hundreds, if not thousands of meters deep. If you lose your footing on your way down, you will most certainly die.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: I heard the mining sites in this territory have had quite a few accidents of late? It's such a small trinket, but the amount of blood spilled for its mining could perhaps fill the knight's bathtub.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Miss Carnelian, I believe you are mistaken...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: For most, these items are indeed difficult to obtain, but they are merely seasonal decorations for Sir Feuerbach.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Such considerations simply do not matter to him.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Whatever his wish is, all he has to do is give the order. That is why we stand here.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Heh...

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Do you perhaps see it differently?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: I'm afraid you wouldn't want to know how I see it.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: With all due respect, Miss Carnelian... You are indebted to the Count's kindness.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Hm.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: The world was shocked when, two years ago, we found an outsider whom none of us have heard of serving the then-underage Count Hohenlohe as his attendant. This has never happened before.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: You should be more careful and consider the Count's position and reputation before you act.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: It sounds like you're not very fond with the way I do things.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: And before you deny it, I've actually met plenty of people who antagonize me as well as those who see the Count as an outsider among the nobles.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: So, am I more or less on point?

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: It is no simple task to have the entire Leithanien be so accepting of an outsider.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: But you don't seem to mind those rumors at all. Certainly, you are no less talented than what the rumors suggest. You are bold as well. Anything I say can only hold you in high esteem.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Hah, you certainly have a way with words, but I will take that as a compliment.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: As for the accident that occurred at the mines... You needn't worry. Our guards and Casters are already on the case.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: You are right. We indeed need to be more careful given the situation. This accident will be dealt with accordingly. No one will be able to use it against the Count.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Oh, you think that's what I'm worried about?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Okay, let's say that's how it is, then. Though, as far as I know, the way you deal with things accordingly isn't generally very peaceful.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: We're merely ridding our blankets of dust.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Oh, so you're saying taking out everyone involved is a way of solving problems?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: It looks like I'm overstaying my welcome. Please excuse me.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Before I go, let me remind you that while Sir Feuerbach is free to ignore the sick in his territory, the Empresses are no gentle little lambs. Looking down on them will not serve you well.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Oh, no no. You must be mistaken, Miss Carnelian, we have never looked down upon the Empresses.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: The Empresses need authority. They need a stronger, authoritative rule. They want to be obeyed, not followed. They have already turned their attention toward us and made the time to deal with us.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Understandable. All rulers eventually walk down this path.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: It's hardly a surprise. We are very familiar with how each other think.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Looks like you are pretty confident.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: You are fearful because you haven't experienced Leithanien's past, Miss Carnelian.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: The Empresses, whether the golden or the black, simply do not compare to the shadows that once shrouded Leithanien.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: And that is despite the fact it was them who overthrew those shadows.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: You are saying...?

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: I lived through that era myself. The red crystals hung high above the towers became a symbol of terror that parents would use it to force their children to behave.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: The Witch King...

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: We don't speak that name these days.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Indeed, I seldom hear of anything on the subject, only some rumors here and there. I heard the legend that a red glow illuminating the entire night sky and how it could be seen all across Leithanien.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: The older generation seems to never have forgotten this, yet they are always mum on the subject.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: This is normal... Aside from trust, fear is also an effective way to silence men.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: I witnessed that sea of red too... And on the second day, the townsmen found that the people of the next town over were all dead. There, dead fowlbeasts were scattered all across the ground, with their feet torn.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: No one knows why. All they know is there were a red glow and the countless corpses it left behind.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: This sounds like a horror story.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Alas, it is also nothing more than a story.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: There exists no reason, no regularity, and no explanation. No one dared to discuss it. Leithanien used to be like that.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Of course, the Empresses' rule is hardly lax either, but we at least know what we are dealing with.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: At the very least, we are not afraid to extend our greetings at balls and banquets unlike that era. We would cower underneath the throne's imposing presence and frightfully worry whether we would be so unfortunate to witness that unreasonableness firsthand.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: It's hard to imagine...

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: It is indeed difficult if you haven't seen it with your own eyes.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: We don't talk about the past anymore. Now... we have a bright future ahead of us all.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: A bright future, huh?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Perhaps you are right. There is much that we can do.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: I wish we'll have a pleasant partnership.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Now please excuse me.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: So this is the Hyacinth Count's exotic attendant.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: The master is eccentric, and the servant is just as crude and bold as the rumors make her.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: How insufferable...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: The air here is still as terrible. It reeks of smoke. Well, it's much better than before, at least.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: The smell of 'progress' and 'advancement.' I'm surprised that I got used to it over the last two years...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: There are men in trendy clothes and shops everywhere. This is no different from any other city center. I'm starting to get sick of seeing this.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: What happened to the normal folks of this city? There's nothing to be appreciated in a song if the tone always stays the same.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Hmm... I guess I've made it to the outskirts?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: (Hm, now that's a change of scenery.)

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: (If I'm not mistaken, that's...)

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: (What should I do...? Hm, I suppose I should contact the 'specialists'—)

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: (This should take care of it.)

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: (Is someone... following me?)

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: (Is it the guards again? No, I can't let them catch me...)

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Looks like things have calmed down.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: It should be okay now that I've come this far outside the city...
Oh? Is that right?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Guard A
steps.text: Did you find them?

steps.name: Guard B
steps.text: No, they didn't come this way!

steps.name: Guard A
steps.text: Keep looking! Those Infected runaways can't be far. Come, this way!

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: T-That was close...

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: I didn't expect them to actually catch up...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: They are the nobles' guards. Hm, there are some traces of Arts too. Perhaps they have a Caster or two.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Um, I'm not sure who you are, but...

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: No need to thank me. It was nothing.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: But it's still too early for you to lower your guard just yet. Those guys aren't that easy to shake. They will still be following you.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Going by your looks, I guess you're not from the city?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Relax. Right, it's not a bad thing to be wary of others, especially given your circumstances.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: I guess... they have been chasing after you for a while?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: How long have you been Infected?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: H-How did you know?!

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: N-No, I'm not infected. You're mistaken.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: I can see the crystals under your collar.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Okay, fasten up. This will do it.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Be more careful next time.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Who are you, and what do you want?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Don't worry, I'm not here to take you away or anything.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Look, if I actually wanted to do anything to you, I could get the job done with much less trouble than the men who are chasing you, and I certainly wouldn't need to stand here and talk to you.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: (That's a good point...)

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Pardon me...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Oh, do you finally believe me? You're starting to sound so formal again.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Uh, I-I'm sorry!

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: No need to apologize. I'm not someone who you need to be so respectful toward, either.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: I've never been a fan of how the Leithanian nobles do things.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: My lady, are you—

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Drop the 'my lady' business.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: But—

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: No buts.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Uh... O-Okay.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Are you not from around here...?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: I'm from Sargon. Have you heard of Sargon?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: What is it like?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: It's very, very far away. And it's a place of freedom.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: There are deserts there, as well as rainforests. Lords ameer big and small lead their own territories, and everyone there gets to live a peaceful life as long as they can pay their tribute. There are also places so remote that you can't find them on maps.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: In those places, we take care of ourselves.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: I've never heard of a place like that.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: That's to be expected.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: When I first came to Leithanien, I even doubted this country existed in the same world as my homeland.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: That sounds so mysterious...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Do you find that hard to believe?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: No, it's just a little hard to imagine.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Haha, I guess it'd be hard to visualize a place when you haven't seen a it with your own eyes.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: (Come to think of it... I said something similar not too long ago.)

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: (I have to admit. The phony noble attendant might just be right.)

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Hmm? Oh... I spaced out again.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: No matter the case, this isn't a safe place to be. The guards will likely be back. We should go somewhere else before I tell you more about Sargon.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Eh? O-Okay!

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Eh?! Is everything you said actually real?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Are there really rivers that flow from the sky and trees larger than whole villages?!

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Of course. There's also a desert that's as tall as the mountains. Walk its golden sands, and you'll find a large hole with countless treasures buried inside...

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Wow!

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: I'm pulling your leg.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Eh?!

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Okay, okay, don't give me that face. I wasn't really pulling your leg. It's a story I heard once. No one knows whether there's any truth to it.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Perhaps they actually have a cave full of jewels and other treasures.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: I hope so...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Ah, this makes me want to go home.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Why don't you go home, then? Is it too far away?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Hm, how should I put it? I hadn't planned on staying, but I ran into some problems, and I got myself tangled up with a troublesome fellow...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: I could've run off, but he definitely wouldn't be able to take care of himself, so I stayed to help him out.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: I thought you said it was a troublesome person? Why are you taking care of him? Have you two become friends?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Hm, I wonder if we're friends. It's a little more complicated than that.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: I'm not sure I get it...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Okay, that's for another time. Looks like the guards didn't come this way. You should be safe here for the moment, but I suggest you leave soon, just to be sure.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Umm, is it okay if I ask you another question?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Are there any Infected in Sargon?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: So they are there too...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: But they don't see the sick people as a scourge to be feared. At least not where I used to live.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: They're just sick, that's all. The beasts in the rainforest kill humans as well, and if you're out gathering fruits and ends up falling from a tree, you could hit your head and die, if you're unlucky. So what makes diseases so terrible?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: That's wonderful...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: It's not all smiles and sugar cubes. Life there is tough in most places. It's because of how tough it is that we don't worry about it so much.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: What about you? Does the lord here send guards after anyone who's infected?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: We didn't used to be like this...

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: My parents worked the mines, and we lived in the area closest to the mining district. A lot of people there have gotten sick.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: All the older folks who work the mines get this disease in the end. Rocks begin to grow on their bodies, but they still have to keep working.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Anyone who has just a bit more money wouldn't ever set foot on our street. Anyone who's not sick yet tries to move out of the area...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: It sounds almost like a quarantine zone.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: A little, but I heard you have to pay to move into the better quarantine zones. They even hand out bread there. That's something that we can only dream of.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: But at least we can live there.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Live how? A mine worker, like your parents, would never step outside your district?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: That isn't so bad... We have a roof over our heads, and we make a small living. That's more than enough to me.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: At least that's what I used to think.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: But then the mines collapsed. My parents didn't come back. The guards sealed off the streets and started rounding up everyone they saw.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: And then no one dared to go outside anymore. Everyone stayed inside, but the guards would also go door to door and force their way in... What have we done wrong?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: (So this is them dealing with it 'accordingly'...)

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: A few kids and I sneaked out of a back alley behind an abandoned building while the guards were distracted. I know the men outside think that anyone who's sick has to die, but I don't want to die!

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: I... I'm scared...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: There, there... Don't cry. Where are the kids you escaped with?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: We made it to this area a couple days ago. There wasn't anywhere we could hide as a group, so we decided to split up.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: That was the last time I saw them, and now I'm all alone...

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: I... I need to find them!

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Calm down, let me—

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Shh, quiet down.

steps.name: Leithanian Caster
steps.text: This way!

steps.name: Leithanian Caster
steps.text: Looks like someone has been here...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: (Calm down. Don't look at him. Breathe slowly...)

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: (Good girl.)

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: (Wait for me here.)

steps.name: Leithanian Caster
steps.text: Finally showing yourself, my lady?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: I'm not one to keep my guests waiting when they come visit with such sincerity.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: You're alone. Where are the guards?

steps.name: Leithanian Caster
steps.text: They needn't be here.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: You sound very confident.

steps.name: Leithanian Caster
steps.text: Lady of Sargon, why are you protecting an Infected?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: No special reason. I met her, and I thought I'd give her a helping hand.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: And what are you after?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: If the goal was simply to be rid of the Infected, they wouldn't need a Caster such as yourself to go through the trouble. You have been capturing the miners for the past two days. What exactly are your orders?

steps.name: Leithanian Caster
steps.text: Are you investigating us?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Nothing so serious. I'm only doing a cursory investigation before we actually sign the contract.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: I wouldn't have figured this out, but I had a little enlightenment earlier today, so I have a good idea of how much Sir Feuerbach has covered up, using you and his guards. Should I perhaps share this with everyone here right now?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: You're quiet. Why so shy? I saw the slaves you were leading away while you were casting. They are Infected, no?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Looks like the dark memories that the Witch King left behind are not merely a thing of the past. Those cruel Arts are still being studied...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Is that what you're capturing the Infected for?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: You're a quiet one. Looks like I found the wrong person to strike a conversation.

steps.name: Leithanian Caster
steps.text: We needn't share a conversation.

steps.name: Leithanian Caster
steps.text: I am merely greeting an Arts user, out of courtesy.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Would you like to get down to business, then? Personally, I prefer to stay out of trouble, but who am I to refuse an opportunity to witness an esteemed Leithanian Caster's skills firsthand?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: (What... are they talking about?!)

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: (Slaves... and research? Is that what they are doing with all the people they caught...?)

steps.name: Leithanian Caster
steps.text: We have no intention of making an enemy of Count Hohenlohe...

steps.name: Leithanian Caster
steps.text: Lady of Sargon, I've heard rumors about you. Your Originium Arts are formidable.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: I guess I should say thanks?

steps.name: Leithanian Caster
steps.text: No need.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: I've never understood you people.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: I see in Leithanien an expanding, overbearing authority. At the same time, I see everyone here worshipping that authority. I've never come to understand why in my two years here.

steps.name: Leithanian Caster
steps.text: You haven't been breathing the air here.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: It's a bit too smoggy for my taste.

steps.name: Leithanian Caster
steps.text: In that case, you will suffocate. It is the fate of all those who breathe foreign air.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: You make that sound like some kind of curse.

steps.name: Leithanian Caster
steps.text: If you wish to die to strange witchcraft, I suggest you try a Sarkaz, of an ancient bloodline.

steps.name: Leithanian Caster
steps.text: It's not part of our plan to fight you here... You may have the Infected hiding there.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Oh, that's music to my ears. Here I was racking my brain thinking how to keep your screams down... I wouldn't want this to cause any problems in our partnership.

steps.name: Leithanian Caster
steps.text: Hmph, arrogant foreigner. I can overlook this, but do not forget...

steps.name: Leithanian Caster
steps.text: Leithanien has its own rules, and the rules here do not bend to any one person.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: He's gone. I'm so glad we didn't actually end up fighting. I wouldn't want to ruin anything and get my ears pinned back by the little Count.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: It's okay. You can come out—

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Hm? Why are you so quiet? Did that scare you?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Look at what a crybaby you are... You are so much more timid than my little sister.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: I'm not scared...!

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: It's just... I heard what you two just said...

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: What will happen to everyone they took away?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Do you want me to lie to make you feel better?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Okay. If you want to hear the truth, I guess all I can tell you is things aren't looking great for them.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: The nobles here want to make everything here 'go away.' That's both the accident in the mine and the workers there. Whether they were caught by the Casters or the guards, things don't bode well for them.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: This is what you wanted to know.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Why...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Oh, don't cry. I'm not good around girls your age, crying their eyes out.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: What will you do now? Are you going to look for your friends?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: R-Right! I shouldn't cry yet. I need to find the others...!

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: If... If the nobles here won't have us, we'll leave this place behind... and go somewhere else! I'm older than all of them. I'm the big sister. I need to protect them...

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: And... one day... I'll avenge the people in the neighborhood...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: You'll leave this place? Even if you have to leave your homeland?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Even if I... have to leave everything behind.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: I don't have much left anyway.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: You're right about that...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Okay, if that's how you feel, there's someone much better suited for the task than me.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: You can come on out too. Enough hiding, my 'specialist.'

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Sheesh... You make that sound like I meant to hide. Can't you let me make a decent entrance?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: My bad, but your footsteps were pretty loud. Asking me to pretend I didn't hear that just to give you a nice entrance is a pretty tall order.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Maybe that says something about what big ears you got, then.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: I'll take that as a compliment.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: That's not a... Whatever.

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: I-Is this person... a specialist?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Don't listen to her. My job is nothing that glamorous. I'm just a—

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Aren't you guys specialists that handle Infected problems? That's how you introduced yourselves, if I remember correctly.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Don't forget you are one of us.

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Ah... Yeah, I know.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: (So half-hearted!)

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: (Hey, now. Don't make a fuss about everything. Anyway, everything's as you can see. Can I leave the girl to you people?)

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: (Well, no problem with that.)

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: (Considering your standing... It's not a good idea to bring her with you.)

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: (My, how dependable.)

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: (Stop playing with me already. That's another girl putting on the weeps because of you. How many times has it been?)

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: (I really don't get it. You keep saying you can't stir up any trouble, but you keep running into trouble head on every time.)

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: (Haha, I wonder why. I'm not so sure.)

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: (I'm just doing things according to my principles...)

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Excuse me...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Will we... meet again?

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Carnelian
steps.text: As long as you stay true to your beliefs now, I'm sure we will.
Those who are humble will always say, 'This is where I belong.'
Those who are egotistical will say, 'This place belongs to me.'
Life in Sargon is shaped by the shifting sands. Here stands a woman of Sargon who is certainly not an egotist, but definitely not humble either.
If you must change who you are to fit in, there is no need.
You needn't fit in.
Be yourself.
